# Scoring API reference

HTTP routes, request fields, decision schemas, response envelopes, and body limits.

Source: [site documentation](https://web-production-c0739.up.railway.app/docs/api-reference) · platform revision `4b7879729687067d55fe230a0503385b205c0018`.

<a id="routes"></a>

## Data plane routes

All paths below are relative to https://api-production-761a5.up.railway.app/api/antibot. Requests use JSON. Server endpoints require both X-Site-Key and X-Secret-Key; browser endpoints use X-Site-Key and an allowlisted Origin.

| Method / path | Authentication | Body / result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| POST /fingerprint | Public | {fingerprint, behavior?} → token and device_id. |
| POST /collect | Public | VerificationRequest → decision. Observes request IP and user agent. |
| POST /events/batch | Public | {events: VerificationRequest[]} → per-item results. |
| POST /challenge | Public | {difficulty?} → challenge. |
| POST /challenge/verify | Public | {challenge_id, nonce} → proof validity. |
| POST /verify | Private | VerificationRequest → decision. |
| POST /verify/fingerprint | Private | {fingerprint, behavior?} → token and device_id. |
| POST /verify/batch | Private | {events: VerificationRequest[]} → per-item results. |
| POST /verify/challenge | Private | {difficulty?} → challenge. |
| POST /verify/challenge/verify | Private | {challenge_id, nonce} → proof validity. |

**bash**

```bash
curl -X POST 'https://api-production-761a5.up.railway.app/api/antibot/verify' \
  -H "X-Site-Key: $BASTION_SITE_KEY" \
  -H "X-Secret-Key: $BASTION_SECRET_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "idempotency_key":"checkout-order_123-v1",
    "context":{
      "event_type":"checkout",
      "account_id":"customer_123",
      "order_amount":129.00,
      "payment_hash":"pm_provider_identifier"
    }
  }'
```

This server-only curl example omits browser telemetry for brevity. A production browser integration should forward the complete buildRequest result. A context-only verification has less evidence available.

<a id="request"></a>

## VerificationRequest fields

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| context | object · required | Authoritative event and account context. |
| token | string · optional | Registered fingerprint token, site-bound and valid for 10 minutes. |
| fingerprint | object · optional | Device evidence collected by the browser SDK. |
| behavior | object · optional | Interaction metrics and bounded samples. |
| environment | object · optional | Browser environment, timestamp, and freshness evidence. |
| headers | string map · optional | Supply only actual observed headers from your trusted server boundary. |
| username | string · optional | Display context for the account. |
| idempotency_key | string · optional | 1–128 characters: letters, numbers, underscore, period, colon, hyphen. SDKs generate one when absent. |

| context field | Type | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| event_type | string · required | signup, login, promo_claim, checkout, or page_view. |
| account_id | string · required | Nonempty external account identifier; keep stable across events. |
| email | string · optional | Customer email from your trusted account record. |
| order_amount | number · optional | Finite nonnegative server-validated amount. Use a consistent currency convention for your site. |
| payment_hash | string · optional | Stable provider payment identifier or hash; never a raw card number. |
| promo_code | string · optional | Promo identifier, validated by your application. |
| ip_address / user_agent | string · optional | Actual client values observed at a trusted proxy/application boundary. |
| request_url | string · optional | Associated application URL. |
| login_succeeded | boolean · optional | Only after your server validates credentials. Browser claims are stripped. |

<a id="response"></a>

## Response envelope & decision

Successful JSON responses use {success: true, data, timestamp}. SDKs unwrap data. Treat any 2xx response as an HTTP success; Nest POST routes generally return 201. This example is illustrative evidence, not a guaranteed result for the sample request.

**decision.json**

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "classification": "suspicious",
    "risk_score": 48,
    "risk_level": "medium",
    "action": "review",
    "request_id": "req_example",
    "device_id": "fp_example",
    "signals": [
      {
        "rule": "device_reuse",
        "score": 20,
        "description": "Device fingerprint is shared by multiple accounts."
      }
    ],
    "identity": {
      "cluster_id": "cluster_example",
      "linked_accounts": 3,
      "shared_devices": 1,
      "shared_ips": 1,
      "shared_payments": 0
    },
    "decision_ms": 14.2,
    "timestamp": "2026-10-14T12:00:00.000Z"
  },
  "timestamp": "2026-10-14T12:00:00.000Z"
}
```

| Decision field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| classification | human, suspicious, or bot. |
| risk_score / risk_level | 0–100 score; low <30, medium 30–59, high 60–84, critical 85–100. |
| action | allow, review, challenge, or block. Enforce this server policy result. |
| request_id / device_id | Recorded decision identifier and device fingerprint identifier. |
| signals | Array of {rule, score, description}; preserve evidence in your audit trail. |
| identity | Optional linked-account/shared-device/IP/payment counts; plan-gated. |
| challenge | Optional proof-of-work challenge descriptor. |
| decision_ms / timestamp | Scoring duration and decision time. |

<a id="limits"></a>

## Payload limits

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Single scoring HTTP body | 256 KiB. |
| Batch HTTP body | 5 MiB; 1–50 events. |
| Per-event engine input | 256 KiB. |
| Behavior samples | At most 2,048 total; SDK collection is further bounded. |
| Other management HTTP bodies | 100 KiB. |
| Fingerprint token | 10 minutes; bound to the site. |

Malformed JSON returns 400 and oversized bodies return 413. Batch HTTP success does not mean every item was accepted. See the batch and error guides for recovery behavior.
